newsitem.title: USA: Ashland Coal to merger with Arch Mineral.
newsitem.headline: Ashland Coal to merger with Arch Mineral.

text.p: Ashland Coal Inc on Friday said it signed a definitive agreement with Arch Mineral Corp to merge in a tax-free reorganization.

Ashland said its shareholders would receive one share of the company to be formed from the merger for every common share held in Ashland. Those with Class B and Class C convertible preferred stock will get 20,500 shares of common stock for each preferred share held.
It said Ashland Inc, which already owns "significant interests" in Ashland Coal and Arch Mineral, will own about 53 percent of the new company.
It did not reveal the value or other terms of the deal and one of its officials declined to comment.
Ashland said the merger will likely raise cash flow per share almost immediately and earnings per share in 1999.
"We believe the shareholders of both companies will realize significant benefits from this merger," it said.
Ashland said the new company, Arch Coal Inc, will be a platform for expansion through acquisitions and internal growth. Its shares are expected to be listed on the New York Stock Exchange, it added.

Ashland's chairman, president and chief executive officer, William Payne, is to retire after the merger, while Steven Leer, president and chief executive officer of Arch Mineral, will become president and chief executive officer of the new company, it said.
John Hall, retired chairman and chief executive officer of Ashland and member of Arch Mineral's board of minerals, will become chairman of the new company, it added.
The new company, whose head offices will be in St. Louis, will have about two billion tons of coal reserves and assets totalling nearly $1.7 billion, Ashland said.
Once the merger is complete, the new company have about 39.6 million shares of common stock outstanding, it said.

"Including the 694,035 shares issuable upon exercise of employee stock options held by Ashland Coal employees, the shareholders of Arch Mineral would own approximately 52 percent of Arch Coal and the shareholders of Ashland Coal would own approximately 48 percent," it said.
Ashland Coal mines and processes low-sulfur coal, while Arch Mineral mines and processes bituminous coal.
